exact_action_boundary.proposal_effect: The proposal would require the Department of Homeland Security to withhold its funds from a college or university that has a covered contract, agreement, gift, or in-kind donation unless the relationship ends or the Secretary grants a qualifying waiver.

limitations: The proposal concerns Department of Homeland Security funds, not all federal education funding, and defines the covered relationships and entities in the bill.

mechanism.description: A Department of Homeland Security funding restriction, lifted when the institution ends the covered relationship, with renewable one-year national-security waivers and congressional notice.

approved_action_meanings.plain_language_meaning: Colleges and universities with specified financial or contractual ties to named China-linked programs or entities would generally lose eligibility for Department of Homeland Security funding. A time-limited waiver would be available when the stated safeguards and national-security conditions are met.

exact_action_boundary.proposal_effect: The proposal would require the centers to inform small businesses about hiring career-and-technical-education graduates, tell students and graduates about center services for starting or expanding a business, and make appropriate connections between businesses and programs.

limitations: The measure changes Small Business Act program duties; it does not create a general education or workforce-spending program.

mechanism.description: Amendments to the Small Business Act duties of small business development centers and women's business centers.

approved_action_meanings.plain_language_meaning: Federal small-business assistance centers would add outreach linking employers with career-and-technical-education graduates and informing those students and graduates about help starting or growing a small business.

exact_action_boundary.proposal_effect: The proposal would require a covered school to submit a written disclosure identifying the foreign source, amounts, and applicable terms within 30 days after receiving funds or entering contracts above the $10,000 aggregate threshold.

limitations: The $10,000 trigger is measured in the aggregate for funds from, or contracts with, a foreign source as specified by the bill.

mechanism.description: A condition on federal financial assistance requiring school disclosures to the Secretary of Education within 30 days.

approved_action_meanings.plain_language_meaning: Public K–12 schools receiving federal education assistance would have to report foreign funding and contracts above an aggregate $10,000 threshold to the Department of Education within 30 days, including the source and relevant terms.

exact_action_boundary.proposal_effect: The proposal would generally prohibit covered federal education funds for a school that partners with a Chinese-government-funded cultural or language institute, operates a supported learning center, or receives specified teaching materials, personnel, funds, or other resources from someone acting for that government. The Secretary could waive the prohibition for a qualifying pre-enactment contract from the prohibition's effective date through contract termination.

limitations: The restriction applies to the bill's defined federal education programs and covered forms of support, not every school resource or foreign relationship.

The waiver is discretionary, not automatic: a covered contract must take effect before enactment and continue beyond the prohibition's effective date. The school must timely submit the complete unredacted contract, an English translation if needed, and a statement demonstrating benefit to its mission and students and promotion of U.S. security, stability, and economic vitality.

mechanism.description: A prohibition on funds under covered federal education programs, effective one year after enactment, with discretionary Secretary of Education waivers for qualifying pre-enactment contracts until those contracts terminate.

approved_action_meanings.plain_language_meaning: K–12 schools would generally lose access to covered federal education funds if they maintain specified partnerships or receive specified resources backed directly or indirectly by the Chinese government. Schools with qualifying pre-existing contracts could receive a waiver lasting until the contract ends.

exact_action_boundary.proposal_effect: The proposal would require funded schools to let parents review specified foreign-funded curricular or staff-development materials and, within 30 days of a request, disclose covered staff compensation, donations, written agreements, and financial transactions; schools would also publish notice of these rights each year.

limitations: The disclosure rights cover the foreign sources and materials defined by the bill and remain subject to copyright law.

mechanism.description: A condition on Elementary and Secondary Education Act funding requiring local educational agencies and schools to answer parent requests and publish annual notice of those rights.

approved_action_meanings.plain_language_meaning: Schools receiving federal K–12 funds would have to give parents a defined way to inspect materials and obtain information about specified foreign funding and agreements, with 30-day response deadlines and annual public notice.

exact_action_boundary.proposal_effect: The proposal would extend secure payments to eligible states and counties through fiscal year 2026, require adjustments where earlier 25-percent payments overlap with fiscal years 2024 or 2025 payments, and extend county project and resource-advisory-committee authorities.

limitations: The measure extends a federal-land and county-payment program; it is not a general education-funding program.

mechanism.description: Date extensions and payment-adjustment rules in the Secure Rural Schools and Community Self-Determination Act, plus extension of resource-advisory-committee authority.

approved_action_meanings.plain_language_meaning: The federal-land county-payment program would continue through fiscal year 2026, with rules reconciling earlier payments and continuing related local project and advisory-committee authorities.

exact_action_boundary.proposal_effect: The proposal would nullify EO14251's removal of named agencies and subdivisions from the federal civil-service labor-management statute and specified State Department and USAID units from the Foreign Service labor-management statute. Nullification would also remove this order's delegations and its directions to end specified agency participation in labor proceedings and reassign employees from non-agency business after agreement termination. Federal funds could not implement the order, and covered agency-union agreements in effect on March 26, 2025 would remain effective through their stated terms.

limitations: Title 5 exclusions cover State, Defense, Treasury except the Bureau of Engraving and Printing, Veterans Affairs, Justice, Energy except FERC, EPA, USAID, NRC, NSF, USITC, FCC, and GSA. They also cover listed HHS, DHS, Interior and Agriculture units, Commerce's International Trade Administration, and specified information-resource-management offices across executive departments, SSA and OPM. The exact subdivisions are retained in the structured source excerpts, not generalized to all employees of every listed department.

The order retains Chapter 71 coverage for immediate local employing offices of police officers, security guards and firefighters, except the Bureau of Prisons, and for specified Marshals Service subdivisions. Defense and VA secretaries could restore coverage to subdivisions through certified orders submitted for Federal Register publication within 15 days. Transportation received a separate, non-redelegable power to exclude subdivisions, including FAA, or suspend provisions for certain overseas activities after published determinations; the order does not itself exclude every Transportation employee.

Foreign Service exclusions cover State subdivisions under the named senior offices plus embassies, consulates, diplomatic missions and consular offices, and USAID overseas missions/field offices and specified administrator/deputy-administrator subdivisions. The complete lists are in EO14251 section 3's structured excerpts.

The order's directions about non-agency business and pending grievances, arbitral-award exceptions and unfair-labor-practice proceedings apply to affected employees upon termination of their agreements. Its 30-day agency-review report is ancillary to this action explanation. This candidate addresses what the bill would undo in this named order, not current agency execution, litigation outcomes, other orders, or a claim that all earlier labor exclusions disappear.

mechanism.description: H.R.2550 would give the March 27, 2025 order no force or effect and prohibit implementation funding. The order excludes named bodies from Title 5 Chapter 71 and specified State/USAID subdivisions from Title 22 Chapter 52 Subchapter X labor-management coverage, with exceptions and delegated powers. The bill separately keeps March 26, 2025 agency-union agreements effective through their stated terms.
mechanism.type: executive-order nullification, funding prohibition, and agreement preservation

approved_action_meanings.plain_language_meaning: The bill would cancel the order excluding major federal departments and specified other agencies or units from statutory labor-management coverage, including collective-bargaining arrangements, and excluding specified State Department and USAID units from the Foreign Service system. It would bar spending to implement that order and separately preserve covered union agreements already in effect on March 26, 2025 until their stated end dates.

exact_action_boundary.proposal_effect: The proposal would extend the limitations period for listed criminal and civil fraud actions involving covered pandemic unemployment claims to ten years and rescind $5 million in unobligated funds.

limitations: The extension applies only to the statutes and pandemic unemployment programs listed in the bill and does not revive a case whose limitations period had already expired before enactment.

mechanism.description: CARES Act amendments creating ten-year enforcement periods for specified fraud offenses, paired with a $5 million rescission.

approved_action_meanings.plain_language_meaning: Authorities would have up to ten years to bring the specified fraud cases tied to named pandemic unemployment programs, and the bill would cancel $5 million in unused funding.

exact_action_boundary.proposal_effect: Institutions would report by July 31 of the following year when gifts and contracts from one foreign source reach $100,000 in a calendar year or $250,000 over the previous three calendar years. Institutions substantially owned or controlled by foreign sources would report annually, including foreign gifts and contracts regardless of value; restricted or conditional gifts and contracts require additional disclosures. The Secretary would publish searchable, downloadable reports within 60 days of submission, allow equivalent state or federal reports and corrections, and could impose specified fines or compliance plans for noncompliance. Defined payments and transactions are excluded. Negotiated rules must address research-security reporting alignment, confidentiality, affiliated entities, structured gifts and contracts, and national-security-risk research; the rewritten disclosure section becomes effective with those rules.

limitations: This is the printed substitute amendment, not the parent bill's meaning. It replaces page 1, line 1 through page 60, line 6; adoption at the amendment stage would not itself enact the substitute.

Reports identify amounts, source/country and purpose or intended use. Institutions must retain agreement copies until the latest of four years after agreement, termination, or applicable state retention requirements; produce them for audits or investigations; and translate contracts as applicable. Restricted or conditional gifts also require amounts, dates, conditions, and specified source-country information.

A state or other federal report can replace the disclosure report only if it contains all required information for the same or an equivalent period; state assurances may be required. Institutions must be able to revise past reports to correct errors.

For a knowing or willful disclosure or agreement-copy/translation violation, the Secretary may impose $250 to 50% of the gift or contract amount; three consecutive years permit an additional fine of $100,000 to the gift or contract amount. Knowing or willful foreign-ownership-report violations can incur up to 25% of Higher Education Act funding excluding Title IV student aid, with an additional fine subject to the same 25% cap for three consecutive years of violations. Administrative errors lasting three consecutive years can incur $250 to 50% of the gift or contract amount; two consecutive years without the required gift/contract report can trigger a compliance plan. These are the printed statutory bounds, not a prediction of penalties imposed.

Excluded transactions include student-attendance payments or scholarships from a natural person acting individually, not for another person or entity except the student, without another contract beyond the institution-student attendance agreement; specified intellectual-property licensing or technical assistance not identified as a national-security risk; and funds solely for clinical trials. A U.S.-located institution's purchases of property or services from a foreign source are outside the contract definition. Gifts and contracts through an institution's supporting entities are included. Restricted or conditional gifts/contracts include terms concerning faculty employment, academic or research units/programs, student selection/admission, or aid restricted by the listed country, religion, sex, ethnic-origin or political-opinion categories.

The amendment also incorporates HEA487(e)(2)(B)(ii) gift exceptions: loan/default-prevention/financial-literacy materials and programs; qualifying professional-training food, refreshments and materials; comparable student-employee loan benefits; institution-controlled, non-promotional loan counseling; specified lender/servicer/guarantor philanthropy or contributions without a loan-related advantage; and state-administered education aid. These categories retain the conditions in the incorporated statute, governed here in its 2024 U.S. Code edition.

Institutions must designate a compliance officer, and the Department must maintain an internal, conflict-free contact for compliance assistance and database improvements. Data sharing with outside persons, including political appointees and personnel detailed from other agencies, is limited to expressly authorized or public information. Database user-group composition and meeting mechanics are ancillary to the explanation, not absent from the governed evidence.

Negotiated rules must align with other agencies' reporting under the CHIPS Act, the Research and Development, Competition, and Innovation Act, and OSTP guidance including the specified NSPM-33 implementation guidance. Alignment is a rulemaking duty, not an assertion that all reporting regimes become identical. The substitute links Section 117's effective date to the regulations and separately specifies a database deadline relative to the first July 31 after enactment; this candidate does not invent a resolution of that timing interaction.

mechanism.description: The amendment would replace the bill's text and rewrite Higher Education Act Section 117. It would set reporting thresholds and deadlines, a public database, alternative-report and correction procedures, compliance responsibilities, financial sanctions, and defined exclusions; the Secretary must begin negotiated rulemaking within one year, and the rewritten Section 117 takes effect when those regulations take effect.
mechanism.type: substitute amendment: disclosure duties, exceptions, fines, and negotiated rulemaking

approved_action_meanings.plain_language_meaning: This substitute would require colleges to report foreign gifts and contracts at $100,000 in one year or $250,000 over three years from the same source, while requiring broader disclosures from institutions substantially owned or controlled by foreign sources and for restricted gifts. Reports would become publicly searchable, equivalent state or federal reports could substitute, and specified noncompliance could bring fines or a compliance plan. The proposal includes payment and transaction exclusions and requires negotiated rules to coordinate reporting with other federal research-security requirements before the rewritten disclosure section takes effect.

exact_action_boundary.proposal_effect: The package would require new reports on covered foreign gifts, contracts, individual relationships, and investments; prohibit institutions from entering specified contracts with foreign countries or entities of concern unless waived; and establish investigation, civil-enforcement, and compliance duties.

limitations: This was a vote on the whole package. The candidate does not attribute the House action to any one component or to H.Amdt. 12.

mechanism.description: Higher Education Act amendments imposing institution and individual disclosures, prohibiting specified contracts subject to waivers, requiring investment reports, and establishing federal enforcement procedures.
mechanism.type: whole-package reporting duties, contract prohibition, waivers, and enforcement

approved_action_meanings.plain_language_meaning: Colleges and universities would face expanded reporting and compliance rules for specified foreign money, contracts, individual ties, and investments. The package would also bar specified contracts unless a waiver applied and create enforcement procedures for noncompliance.

exact_action_boundary.proposal_effect: Funded public schools would have to obtain parental consent before changing a covered minor's gender markers, pronouns or preferred name on a school form, or sex-based accommodations such as bathrooms or locker rooms. Separately, ESEA funds could not be used to teach or advance concepts related to the incorporated EO14168 definition: gender identity replacing sex as a category, people identifying as a gender different from their sex, a spectrum of genders disconnected from sex, and the concept of being born in the wrong-sexed body. The bill imports that definition from the order rather than creating an independent definition.

limitations: The parental-consent clause is limited to minors in elementary or middle grades and the listed school-form changes or sex-based accommodations. The separate use-of-funds prohibition applies to ESEA funds and is not confined by that clause's definition of a covered student.

EO14168 section 2 defines sex as an unchangeable male/female biological classification and defines gender identity separately; subsection (f) supplies the incorporated gender-ideology definition. That definition also describes requiring institutions to recognize identification as a different sex as establishing that sex. This explanation attributes those classifications to the legal text, without adopting the order's evaluative descriptions or treating its rhetoric as established fact.

The bill prohibits teaching or advancing concepts related to the incorporated definition. It does not enumerate particular lessons, books or classroom scenarios; the candidate does not invent such applications. Incorporating this definition does not import all other Executive Order directives, and this whole-package choice is not projected onto separate component votes.

mechanism.description: The bill conditions ESEA funding for public schools on parental consent for specified changes involving covered minors, and separately amends ESEA's prohibited uses of funds. That prohibition incorporates EO14168 section 2's definition, which concerns replacing sex as a category with self-assessed gender identity, identifying as a gender different from one's sex, and a spectrum of genders disconnected from sex.
mechanism.type: parental-consent funding condition and separate use-of-funds prohibition by incorporated definition

approved_action_meanings.plain_language_meaning: Public schools receiving ESEA funds would need parental consent for specified school-form or bathroom/locker-room changes involving minors in elementary or middle grades. A separate rule would bar ESEA-funded teaching or advancement of concepts covered by EO14168's definition of gender ideology, including identity replacing sex as a category, identifying as a gender different from one's sex, a spectrum of genders separate from sex, and being born in the wrong-sexed body. These are the Executive Order's incorporated categories, not Political Fingerprint's judgments about gender.

exact_action_boundary.proposal_effect: The proposal would permit employers to exclude education or training time from hours worked when it occurs outside regular hours, participation is voluntary without adverse action for declining, and no work is performed; it would also permit exclusion of qualifying supplemental apprenticeship instruction.

limitations: The governed source is the official House-section Congressional Record at H677-H678 because no House-engrossed text exists for the failed passage; floor advocacy is not used as semantic evidence.

mechanism.description: An amendment to federal wage-and-hour rules defining when education or training time may be excluded from hours worked.
mechanism.type: Fair Labor Standards Act hours-worked exclusion

approved_action_meanings.plain_language_meaning: Specified voluntary training outside regular work hours would not have to count as paid working time when the bill's conditions were met. Qualifying supplemental classroom instruction connected to a bona fide apprenticeship could also be excluded.

exact_action_boundary.proposal_effect: The proposal would require maintaining current wages, hours, and terms and conditions of employment pending agreement and continuing an employer's bargaining duty unless the representative is decertified following an election. For first contracts, the parties must begin bargaining within 10 days of a written request; after 90 days of bargaining without agreement either party could request federal mediation, and after 30 days from that request without agreement the dispute would go to arbitration. The parties may agree to longer periods, and the panel's award would bind them for two years unless amended by their written consent.

limitations: The timetable applies to initial collective-bargaining agreements; the employment-term maintenance and continuing bargaining duties are separate amendments to the general bargaining provision. The candidate does not predict when agreement would be reached or what terms would result.

Section 4's GAO report on the time from recognition or certification to a first contract is treated as ancillary and non-material to this action explanation; it is omitted from the operative synthesis.

mechanism.description: National Labor Relations Act amendments requiring current wages, hours, and employment terms to be maintained pending agreement and continuing an employer's bargaining duty absent decertification following an election. First-contract bargaining must begin within 10 days, mediation may be requested after 90 days without agreement, and unresolved disputes go to a three-person arbitration panel 30 days after the mediation request, subject to agreed extensions.
mechanism.type: employment-term maintenance, continuing bargaining duty, deadlines, and binding arbitration

approved_action_meanings.plain_language_meaning: Current wages, hours, and employment terms would have to be maintained while an agreement is pending, and employers would have to keep bargaining unless an election removes the employee representative's certification. First-contract talks would start within 10 days of a written request, allow mediation after 90 days without agreement, and move to arbitration after 30 days from the mediation request, subject to agreed extensions. The arbitration award would bind the parties for two years unless both agreed in writing to amend it.

exact_action_boundary.proposal_effect: The proposal would require the Department of Education to screen each covered FAFSA, notify flagged applicants and their selected schools, and require a school to verify identity by an approved method before disbursing federal student aid; repeated noncompliant disbursements would become a program-review priority.

limitations: A reasonable-suspicion flag triggers verification and notice; the proposal does not itself establish that the applicant committed fraud.

mechanism.description: Higher Education Act requirements for Department screening, applicant and school notices, institutional identity verification before disbursement, records, guidance, reports, and program-review prioritization.
mechanism.type: screening, notification, verification, and program-review duties

approved_action_meanings.plain_language_meaning: Every FAFSA filed from October 1, 2026 would be screened for indicators of identity fraud. If an application were flagged, a college could not release federal aid until it completed an approved identity check and notified the Department.

exact_action_boundary.proposal_effect: The package would require retirement-plan investment decisions generally to rest on financial risk and return, prohibit sacrificing return or taking extra risk for nonfinancial goals, require provider selection without regard to race, color, religion, sex, or national origin, require shareholder-rights decisions to serve financial interests, and require notices before transactions outside the plan's designated investment options.

limitations: The investment rule allows documented nonfinancial tie-breakers when financial factors cannot distinguish alternatives, subject to the bill's conditions. This is an indivisible whole-package choice across four divisions; the candidate does not attribute the House action to any single component.

mechanism.description: Employee Retirement Income Security Act amendments plus a Government Accountability Office study requirement.
mechanism.type: whole-package fiduciary requirements, prohibitions, disclosures, and study

approved_action_meanings.plain_language_meaning: Private retirement-plan managers would generally have to base investments and shareholder-rights decisions on financial interests, while following new provider-selection rules. Participants using investments outside the plan's designated options would receive required notices, and GAO would compare returns from those arrangements with other plan options.

exact_action_boundary.proposal_effect: The proposal would require covered colleges to provide specified campus and community resource lists, accommodation information, and Title IX complaint instructions through annual emails and designated student-information channels.

limitations: The bill states that it does not authorize the Secretary to require additional information or create additional rights beyond those listed.

mechanism.description: A Higher Education Act condition requiring annual email, handbook, orientation, health or counseling center, and public-website dissemination.

approved_action_meanings.plain_language_meaning: Colleges in federal student-aid programs would have to tell prospective and enrolled students where pregnant students carrying a pregnancy to term can find specified resources and accommodations and how to file certain discrimination complaints.

exact_action_boundary.proposal_effect: The proposal would prohibit a covered public college from charging a qualifying resident of one of the four named territories more tuition or fees than it charges residents of the state where the college is located.

limitations: Eligibility is limited to the territorial residents and U.S. nationals defined by the bill and to public institutions receiving assistance under the Higher Education Act.

mechanism.description: A Higher Education Act requirement limiting tuition and fees charged by assisted public institutions.

approved_action_meanings.plain_language_meaning: Qualifying U.S. nationals from Guam, the Northern Mariana Islands, American Samoa, and the U.S. Virgin Islands would receive in-state tuition and fee rates at covered public colleges.

episode_semantic_evidence.single-119-hr-1069-1-313: K–12 schools would generally lose access to covered federal education funds if they maintain specified partnerships or receive specified resources backed directly or indirectly by the Chinese government. Schools with qualifying pre-existing contracts could receive a waiver lasting until the contract ends.
episode_semantic_evidence.single-119-hr-881-1-120: Colleges and universities with specified financial or contractual ties to named China-linked programs or entities would generally lose eligibility for Department of Homeland Security funding. A time-limited waiver would be available when the stated safeguards and national-security conditions are met.

material_limitations: H.R.881 covers higher education and DHS funding; H.R.1069 covers K–12 schools and its defined federal education programs. Neither means all federal funding.

The covered entities and relationships differ. H.R.881's renewable national-security waiver is not H.R.1069's qualifying pre-existing-contract waiver; H.R.1069's prohibition begins one year after enactment.

The relationship concerns these funding exclusions, not opposition to foreign-money disclosure generally. H.R.1048 contains mixed member choices and remains a separate whole-episode notable-choice proposal; H.R.1005 is Not Voting.
proposed_findings.summary: Foushee opposed two proposals making education institutions ineligible for specified federal funds because of covered China-linked relationships, each with a waiver route.

proposed_findings.analytical_value: Tests whether the newly concrete meanings support a useful relationship between preserving existing bargaining coverage and maintaining bargaining obligations. Independent review must decide whether the sector and remedy differences leave enough shared substance.

episode_semantic_evidence.single-119-hr-2550-1-332: The bill would cancel the order excluding major federal departments and specified other agencies or units from statutory labor-management coverage, including collective-bargaining arrangements, and excluding specified State Department and USAID units from the Foreign Service system. It would bar spending to implement that order and separately preserve covered union agreements already in effect on March 26, 2025 until their stated end dates.
episode_semantic_evidence.single-119-hr-5408-2-216: Current wages, hours, and employment terms would have to be maintained while an agreement is pending, and employers would have to keep bargaining unless an election removes the employee representative's certification. First-contract talks would start within 10 days of a written request, allow mediation after 90 days without agreement, and move to arbitration after 30 days from the mediation request, subject to agreed extensions. The arbitration award would bind the parties for two years unless both agreed in writing to amend it.

material_limitations: H.R.2550 concerns specified federal and Foreign Service bodies and an executive order; H.R.5408 amends the NLRA system. Their workers, statutory regimes and legal tools are different.

Keeping existing federal union agreements effective through their terms differs from maintaining employment terms pending agreement and continuing a bargaining duty. The proposed shared relationship is continuity of bargaining, not identical contract protection.
H.R.5408 also mandates a first-contract timetable and binding arbitration. H.R.2550 does not. Support for either whole measure cannot be assigned exclusively to its continuity provisions.

EO14251's agency subdivisions, exceptions and delegated powers remain bounded by the approved action limitations. This is not a claim about all federal employees, actual litigation outcomes, or a general pro-labor position.
proposed_findings.summary: Across two different labor systems, Foushee supported keeping collective bargaining in force during potential disruptions. She voted to restore bargaining coverage and preserve existing agreements for specified federal workers, and separately voted to require continued bargaining and unchanged employment terms while newly represented workers pursued a first contract.

proposed_findings.analytical_value: The newly supported substitute meaning makes the within-episode contrast substantively legible without treating every directional action as independently notable.

episode_semantic_evidence.hr-1048-amendment-and-final-passage:
This substitute would require colleges to report foreign gifts and contracts at $100,000 in one year or $250,000 over three years from the same source, while requiring broader disclosures from institutions substantially owned or controlled by foreign sources and for restricted gifts. Reports would become publicly searchable, equivalent state or federal reports could substitute, and specified noncompliance could bring fines or a compliance plan. The proposal includes payment and transaction exclusions and requires negotiated rules to coordinate reporting with other federal research-security requirements before the rewritten disclosure section takes effect.
Colleges and universities would face expanded reporting and compliance rules for specified foreign money, contracts, individual ties, and investments. The package would also bar specified contracts unless a waiver applied and create enforcement procedures for noncompliance.

material_limitations: The substitute would replace the printed text with its own thresholds, public reports, exclusions, fines and negotiated-rulemaking duties. Its reporting requirements are not inferred from the parent bill.

The final package includes institution and individual disclosures, specified contract prohibitions with waivers, investment reports and enforcement. The Nay vote applies to the whole package; it does not establish opposition to any one component.

The amendment failed in the House and the final package passed the House. Neither outcome establishes enactment. These same-day choices are one episode, not a cross-episode trajectory or a change of position over time.

The paired votes distinguish support for this disclosure substitute from opposition to this final package; they do not establish why Foushee made either choice or a preferred universal disclosure regime.
proposed_findings.summary: Within one H.R.1048 episode, Foushee supported the substitute's threshold-based foreign-gift reporting, exceptions and negotiated rules, then opposed the final package of reporting, contract restrictions and enforcement.
